name: Should I build outward with a ground-floor addition or build upward with a second story?

mainEntity.name: Should I build outward with a ground-floor addition or build upward with a second story?

acceptedAnswer.text: Building out extends your home's foundation outward into your yard, while building up adds a second story on top of your existing structure. Ground-floor additions are generally less disruptive to your daily living environment during construction because crews work outside your current roofline. However, building out consumes yard space and must comply with property setback boundaries. Adding a second story preserves your yard but requires structural evaluation to confirm your existing foundation and framing can support the load, which often means temporarily vacating the space beneath the build.
acceptedAnswer.description: Building outward preserves your interior during construction but uses yard space, while building upward saves lot area but requires verifying existing structural support.
